candidate.title: ChIRP-Seq
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina ChIRP-Seq schematic: RNA-directed capture of crosslinked, fragmented chromatin using biotinylated tiling probes, streptavidin-bead enrichment, RNase-mediated release and DNA extraction. ChIRP (Chromatin Isolation by RNA Purification) is the named capture method underlying this sequencing use, not a separately depicted target workflow. The two initial chromatin illustrations include a title vignette and a workflow starting complex; no alternative route is drawn. The graph ends at extracted DNA as drawn. The cited primary paper is used to interpret the downstream DNA-library/occupancy readout and the RNase simplification, without importing its unshown split-probe experiments, protein/RNA elutions, controls or library-preparation internals.

states.label: Extracted RNA-associated genomic DNA
features: Final depicted material is a single blue line labeled DNA, after DNA extraction; proteins and capture support are no longer drawn.

This genomic DNA is the substrate for downstream sequencing-library construction. The primary paper reports libraries made from ChIRPed DNA; no adapter structures, amplification, RNA-to-cDNA conversion or library-preparation sequence is shown in this schematic.

Sequences in such a DNA library represent genomic fragments co-enriched through the targeted ncRNA and its crosslinked associations. Their genomic mapping supports an RNA-occupancy map, subject to probe artifacts and chromatin preparation effects.

Interpretation: fragment enrichment does not by itself identify the associated protein, distinguish direct RNA–DNA contact from protein-mediated association, or locate a molecular contact at a single nucleotide. The catalogue claims single-base resolution; the inspected evidence supports genomic fragment occupancy without establishing single-nucleotide molecular-contact resolution.

operations.information_effect: Preserves an association between the target ncRNA and genomic fragments for subsequent affinity enrichment; it does not establish a direct molecular contact.
